_note: BuildSkin assembly library. Layers run exterior -> interior. Every value carries a source; null means no source yet (see the matching TODO). Units: thickness_in = inches; k = BTU/(hr*ft*F); cp = BTU/(lb*F); density = lb/ft3; R = h*ft2*F/BTU; U = BTU/(h*ft2*F); heat_capacity = BTU/(ft2*F). Source priority: codes/standards/manufacturer data first; book tables (e.g. Allen & Rand, Architectural Detailing 3rd ed.) only as a last resort, cited by book and table.

reported._u_si_src: Brick Wall.ifc, Pset_WallCommon.ThermalTransmittance. Same value as Revit R converted to SI (not an independent check).
flags: Revit's R treats both air layers as still-air conduction: the 3" air gap and the 6" 'Metal Stud Layer' both use k = 0.0144 (Revit thermal asset 'Air'). That is about R-17.4 + R-34.7 of the R-54.
The 'Metal Stud Layer' material has a steel physical asset (490.06 lb/ft3) but an 'Air' thermal asset, so the steel studs are not in the thermal calculation at all: no steel-stud thermal bridging.
Air-space convection and radiation are ignored (conduction only).
No insulation layer exists in this assembly.
Do not use this R/U for code or LEED compliance. Use effective.u_value once sourced.
reported._layer_check: R from layers with known k: brick 0.968 + air gap 17.361 + stud layer 34.722 = 53.051. The remaining 0.971 is plywood + gypsum (k not yet recorded).
